samples.summary: Specs outside the diff still assume `NODE_ENV` alone decides `Secure`/`__Host-`; the new precedence makes them env-dependent
samples.evidence:
`isSecureCookie()` now consults `COOKIE_SECURE` and `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` *before* `NODE_ENV` (packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts:184-195). The diff recognised the hazard and added `beforeEach(() => delete process.env.GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL)` to `auth.controller.spec.ts:491`, but the sibling specs that assert the same property were not given the same isolation:
- packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.spec.ts:60 (`is __Host- prefixed, secure and path-/ in production`) and :73 (the development case) set only `NODE_ENV`; the new `afterEach` restores `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL`/`COOKIE_SECURE` but nothing clears them first, so an ambient `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL=http://localhost:3000/...` (exactly the value `packages/backend/README.md:41`, `README.md:126` and `packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42` hand out, and that `packages/backend/test/helpers/integration-helpers.ts:93` sets) flips `oauthStateCookieName()` to the unprefixed name and fails the assertion.
- packages/backend/src/auth/cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts:196-221 (`prefixes the confirm cookie with __Host- where cookies are Secure`) does the same with `NODE_ENV=production` only and got no clearing at all.
Effect: green in a bare CI shell, red on a developer machine with the documented env exported — or, worse, quietly asserting nothing about `__Host-` if `COOKIE_SECURE` is set. Fix belongs in these two spec files (mirror the `beforeEach` the diff added to `auth.controller.spec.ts`).
searchedFor: read packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.spec.ts afterEach block in the diff
read packages/backend/package.json jest config (rootDir src, no setupFiles/dotenv)

samples.evidence:
The change makes `command` part of the envelope contract (`packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:158`, docs and `packages/cli/README.md:142` now promise `{"error":{...,"command":"docs.content"}}`), and every action was updated to `outputError(e, this)` — except:
- packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:69 — `outputError(e)`
- packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:85 — `outputError(e)` in `ctx list`, in the very file whose `ctx switch` was reworked for attribution (and whose new test comment claims `ctx list` reports the same condition)
- packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:139 — `outputError(new Error('Invalid JSON cell data…'))` on the stdin/`--data` parse failure
An agent driving several calls gets an unattributed line from exactly these paths.

verdict.reason: Verified the precedence change in isSecureCookie() (oauth-state.ts:184-195: COOKIE_SECURE, then GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL scheme, NODE_ENV last) and confirmed both cited specs still assume NODE_ENV alone decides. oauth-state.spec.ts:59-77 sets only NODE_ENV; its afterEach (lines 16-22) restores GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL/COOKIE_SECURE but never clears them first, so an ambient http:// callback URL (the value handed out by packages/backend/README.md:41 and self-hosting.md:42) makes line 63's __Host- assertion fail, and an ambient COOKIE_SECURE makes line 76 vacuous. cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts:196-221 sets only NODE_ENV with no clearing at all, and cliConfirmCookieName() does route through hostPrefixedCookieName()/useSecureCookies() (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:48-49,61), so the same precedence governs it. I searched widely for the isolation said to be missing and found no counterexample: packages/backend/package.json:100-128 has no setupFiles/setupFilesAfterEach/globalSetup; the only jest config file in the workspace is test/jest-e2e.json (e2e only); a repo-wide grep for delete process.env/setupFiles/globalSetup/dotenv turns up env isolation only in packages/cli/test and frontend vite config. The single backend site with the guard is auth.controller.spec.ts:491-493, whose own comment states this exact hazard, and docs/tasks/active/20260820-pr786-conflict-resolution-todo.md:85-88 records the failure actually happening and being fixed only there. Reachable beyond a shell export too: auth.module.ts:21 calls ConfigModule.forRoot(), which loads .env into the process.env shared by spec files in a jest worker. This is a consumer of the changed contract left env-dependent, not a missing-test complaint, so it sits in the blast-radius lane.

finding.summary: `COOKIE_SECURE` now feeds `cliLoginAvailable`, an out-of-diff consumer of `secureCookies` whose question is "can this origin hold a cookie an attacker cannot plant?" — the override answers a different question and moves that gate in both directions
finding.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:216 `return secureCookies(configService) || loopbackCallback(configService);`, consumed at github-auth.guard.ts:514 to throw `BadRequestException('Command-line sign-in requires an https server')`. Before this delta that predicate was derived from the callback URL scheme only. Now: (a) an operator who sets `COOKIE_SECURE=false` on a genuinely https deployment (e.g. to work around a cookie problem) silently disables `wafflebase login` for every non-loopback deployment — the CLI gets a 400 that names https, on an https server, with no log; (b) `COOKIE_SECURE=true` on a real plain-http origin makes `cliLoginAvailable` return true, starting the CLI consent flow on cleartext where the `wafflebase_cli_confirm` cookie the gate rests on is plantable — the exact case the comment at lines 208-213 says is refused rather than started. The fix belongs on the new code: `cliLoginAvailable` should consult the derived origin scheme, not the operator's cookie-attribute override.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist. `packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts` is 183 lines total — there is no line 216 or 514, no `cliLoginAvailable`, no `loopbackCallback`, no `secureCookies` call, and the file does not import `useSecureCookies` (imports at lines 10-16 are only the cookie-name/options/state helpers). Its sole `BadRequestException` (line 178) is the `Sec-Fetch-Site` cross-site refusal, not an https gate. Repo-wide grep shows `cliLoginAvailable`/`loopbackCallback`/`requires an https` appear nowhere in TypeScript (only in `packages/backend/README.md:120`, `packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:129`, and other agents' `.agent-review/*` files), and `Command-line sign-in` has zero matches in `*.{ts,tsx,js}`. The real `COOKIE_SECURE` consumer chain is `isSecureCookie()` (oauth-state.ts:184-195) -> `useSecureCookies()` (oauth-state.ts:205), whose only non-test call sites are `auth.controller.ts:373` and `cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:61`, both of which use it purely as the cookie `secure` attribute paired with `__Host-` naming. No availability/consent gate consumes it, so there is no out-of-diff consumer left broken and no guard bypassed. (The README/self-hosting prose describing a 400 that no code emits is a genuine docs mismatch, already owned by the docs lens, but it is not the blast-radius defect claimed here.)

finding.summary: Logout's `clearCookie` now inherits `COOKIE_SECURE`, so `COOKIE_SECURE=true` on an origin actually served over http leaves the session cookie in the browser at sign-out
finding.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:474-476 clears `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh` with `this.baseCookieOptions()`, whose `secure` is now `secureCookies()` and therefore operator-settable. A `Set-Cookie` carrying `Secure` sent from a plain-http origin is dropped by the browser, so the expiring cookie never lands and the previously-set session cookie survives logout. The pre-delta derivation could only produce `secure: true` on an origin that had declared itself https; the new override can produce it on an origin that is not. Same class as the `Secure`-on-http dead-login the PR describes, but on the revocation path rather than the login path, so it fails quietly instead of loudly.

verdict.reason: The described code is real, though mis-cited: logout (auth.controller.ts:85-89) does nothing but clearAuthCookies (324-328), which clears wafflebase_session/wafflebase_refresh with baseCookieOptions() whose `secure: useSecureCookies()` (366-376) resolves through oauth-state.ts:205 -> isSecureCookie() (184-195), where COOKIE_SECURE is read first and is therefore operator-settable to true. Logout performs no server-side revocation, so a dropped clearing Set-Cookie does leave a live session. Mitigating facts I checked but could not turn into a concrete refutation: the clear path is symmetric with setAuthCookies (335-349) via the same helper, so there is no bypassing call site; the behaviour is intentionally pinned by auth.controller.spec.ts:504-535; and the triggering state (COOKIE_SECURE=true on a genuinely http origin) also breaks login, making it a documented-escape-hatch misconfiguration (docs/design/backend.md:437-441, self-hosting.md:133-139). A config transition (http deployment later setting COOKIE_SECURE=true with cookies already in browsers) still reaches the failure, and I cannot rule it out, so uncertainty keeps the finding. Note for the author: cited lines 474-476 do not exist (file ends at 377), and the claim that the pre-delta rule could only yield secure:true on an https origin is contradicted by the NODE_ENV fallback at oauth-state.ts:194.
